messages:
cheng: Quick one — for tenant routing do we prefer a signed routing header (X-Tenant-Sign) or derive tenant from the JWT claim? Seeing some clients send custom UA strings that would route them incorrectly. :thinking:
ashley: If we can sign it, signed header wins for trust. JWT claim is fine as fallback but requires consistent auth plumbing across gateways.
priya: Agreed on signed header for customer-controlled routing. But we need a clear fallback order documented in the console so SREs can debug rollouts.
noah: Spoofing risk is real. User-Agent should never be the primary routing key. It can be used for heuristics (e.g. mobile vs desktop) but not tenant. :lock:
cheng: Ok — how about this precedence: 1) X-Tenant-Sign (HMAC-signed by customer key), 2) jwt.claims.tenant, 3) X-Tenant (unsigned) as last-resort? If none, route to default sandbox. Thoughts?
priya: That ordering makes sense. We also need TTL on signatures and replay protection, otherwise old tokens can be reused.
noah: +1 for TTL. Also need a migration plan: many integrations only send X-Tenant today. Console UX should allow temporary opt-in to accept unsigned X-Tenant per route for a time window.
ashley: UX idea: expose a "routing precedence" toggle in route settings with a short explainer and a one-click canary to accept unsigned headers for X days. That'll make rollouts less painful.
cheng: Here's a draft routing rule snippet I mocked for the gateway (pseud YAML):
```
route_match:
  - type: header
    name: X-Tenant-Sign
    signed: true
    verifier: customer-kms://tenant-keys/{tenant}
  - type: jwt_claim
    path: claims.tenant
  - type: header
    name: X-Tenant
    signed: false
fallback: default-sandbox
logging: trace-on-mismatch
```
priya: Looks good. Make sure verifier supports key rotation and logs key id. Also include a warning event if unsigned header is used when customer has signing enabled.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for gateway-rule: tenant-routing-v3 on prod-canary-2 at 2026-08-14T13:24:02Z
noah: One more: telemetry — emit a metric `routing.source` with values [signed_header, jwt, unsigned_header, fallback] so we can alert if unsigned_header > 5% during the opt-in window.
cheng: Nice. I'll update the PR with the precedence, TTL, replay nonce suggestion, and console UX copy. Will also add the telemetry metric.
ashley: Thanks — ping me when PR is ready, I'll review the UX copy. :eyes:
priya: I'll sketch the console mock for the opt-in flow and share in #design.
cheng: Awesome, thanks team.
